question: Why does the single-shoot cross alias on seed 119, and what generator does/doesn't recover truth from a realistic ~1°-off pair?
hypothesis: The pair→ω step has a cheap geometric rule (return-map or LS-peak prior) that picks the right ω; some generator recovers truth from a realistic pair.
narrative_md: The binding blocker is the hard-shoot trap: forcing ω to exactly connect two ~1°-off endpoints over the 3.1-turn A→B baseline bakes in a 4.25° ω-dir error → Band D (RMSE 0.687). The LM multistart generator is sound — on the EXACT truth pair it returns Band A (0.0180, dir-err ~0°). Two shortcuts refuted: the propagator return-map (every direction connects) and LS-peak |ω| priors (band-tiling). Windowing the score (not the objective) also fails. Uses oracle/exact-truth pairs as inputs → not blind.
